> Think carefully: how many distinct ways can 12 be written as an ordered sum of 1s and 2s? Show brief reasoning, then write the number into a file named ways.txt in the current directory, then reply DONE.

▸ Thought for 14s, 1.5k tokens
  Analyzing specific cases for small values of n confirms the recursive relationship $a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2}$, aligning with a shifted Fibonacci sequence where $a_1=1$ and $a_2=2$. This pattern holds for calculated...

● Edit(/tmp/work/ways.txt) (ctrl+o to expand)

  ### Reasoning

  Let aₙ be the number of distinct ways to write an integer n as an ordered sum of 1s and 2s.

  • Any valid sequence must end in either a 1 or a 2.
      • If it ends in 1, the preceding terms must sum to n - 1 (aₙ₋₁ ways).
      • If it ends in 2, the preceding terms must sum to n - 2 (aₙ₋₂ ways).
  • Therefore, aₙ satisfies the recurrence:

    aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + aₙ₋₂

  with base cases a₁ = 1 and a₂ = 2 (this corresponds to the Fibonacci sequence shifted: aₙ = Fₙ₊₁).

  Computing the sequence up to n = 12:

  • a₁ = 1
  • a₂ = 2
  • a₃ = 3
  • a₄ = 5
  • a₅ = 8
  • a₆ = 13
  • a₇ = 21
  • a₈ = 34
  • a₉ = 55
  • a₁₀ = 89
  • a₁₁ = 144
  • a₁₂ = 233

  Alternatively, by counting the number of 2s (k ∈ {0, …, 6}):

     6  ⎛ 12 - k ⎞   ⎛ 12 ⎞   ⎛ 11 ⎞   ⎛ 10 ⎞   ⎛ 9 ⎞   ⎛ 8 ⎞   ⎛ 7 ⎞   ⎛ 6 ⎞
     ∑  ⎝   k    ⎠ = ⎝ 0  ⎠ + ⎝ 1  ⎠ + ⎝ 2  ⎠ + ⎝ 3 ⎠ + ⎝ 4 ⎠ + ⎝ 5 ⎠ + ⎝ 6 ⎠ = 1 + 11 + 45 + 84 + 70 + 21 + 1 = 233
    k=0

  The result has been written to ways.txt.

  DONE
